title: Front Legs, Back Legs
opening_frame: The front half of a pantomime horse kneels heroically while its back legs begin an unwanted tap solo.
question_and_goals: Can two performers finish the children's show without exposing the people inside? The front performer wants to deliver his magnificent heroic scene; the rear performer wants the visiting talent scout to notice his dance skill. Their jobs depend on keeping the illusion through the final curtain.
rule: The costume must remain intact during the show. Their disagreement has to happen through the horse's movements.
causal_escalation: The front tries to plant all four feet for his dramatic speech; the rear keeps the body moving. The front counters with a gallop, accidentally giving the rear a faster dance rhythm. A planned rescue becomes a bucking, moonwalking duel, and both performers must cooperate to keep the child-sized actor playing the princess safely seated on the costume's padded back.
plant_and_payoff: The talent scout's pencil follows the feet, not the speech. Once the curtain falls, the front performer rushes out to claim the applause. The audience calls for the dancing back legs instead. The rear performer gets his own bow, then invites the front performer to supply the back legs of his encore. Their hierarchy has literally reversed.
visual_test: The front and rear must read as separate personalities without dialogue or a cutaway inside the costume. Keep the physical comedy grounded; do not escalate to an unexplained airborne battle.
editorial_note: These are pitches, not approved productions or timed boards. Together with the three fully boarded films above, they make eight topics. They should be developed only if their central visual test works; a striking premise is not yet a finished film.
